chapter: Newark and first years in Harlem
title: Playing the Big Apple in Newark with Joe Crump
summary: He took a job at a rough Newark club under Joe Crump, a gold-toothed leader who could not read music, across from Joe's bordello, while Butler studied classic harmony and counterpoint.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: he says, well, Jack, why don't you go up to the Big Apple and see a man named Professor Jackson, so I says okay, and I went up there and Professor Jackson, couldn't hardly hold the clarinet and so they had another fellow named Joe Crump and Joe Crump had a whole set of gold teeth and had diamonds on each side and this little funny looking place, so he says well, can you play anything so I played the melody and he said, that's nice, so he said can you come to work, and so Jackson said yes, so then come to work tonight and then Jackson disappeared.

Now, that night people, we're playing and it seemed like people started arguing out in the street on the other side of town and they come up there and fight it out and cut it up, so see, Joe couldn't read so I said Joe, now that's F, what do you mean, oh, yes, and right across the street Joe had his bordello right across the street -- well, I won't give you the name of the street -- it was something there --

Yes, something like that and his girl-friends were snatching people so I didn't -- I wanted to know what was happening and Joe was saying now, now, you -- he used to call me Him all the time, so -- I was getting myself together you know, I was learning - and one chick come in there and I'm looking too and he says get away from this bandstand because she had made it possible for another fellow to have died by
request, so she said, after all, I can look and he's nice -- get away from here, and Joe got up and put a little flesh upside that child's head and she didn't come near that bandstand anymore.
So now me and Joe, I'm teaching Joe and he's teaching me that stuff.
Where had you learned the harmony and stuff.
I'm still learning -- I learned in Washington, but he moved to Newark, New Jersey. I studied there, I had gotten my book.

Classic harmony and then I mess with the counterpoint, but I had no place to use it and in fact, recognize what I heard, so I stayed up there and one day they said, have you heard. They said, what happened, Joe was found in bed with the singer, and the husband come in and hit Joe in the head with some iron pipes. I said, what. So that night come on the job with some vaseline on his head. There's a little abrasion so he said let's play, let's go, everything was all right.
